column7: 2026-11-06: Storage team decision: in parseBytes on this branch, units without the 'i' (KB/kB, MB, GB...) are powers of 1024 (Windows Explorer style): '1 KB' and '1 kB' = 1024, '1 MB' = 1048576. Not implemented yet; they currently throw 'Unsupported unit' (test 'decimal units are not supported yet' must be replaced). Do not read them as powers of 1000. Binary units (KiB..YiB) done and committed.

2026-11-06: billing-svc: parseBytes accepts only plain numbers, B and KiB..YiB; kB/MB/GB etc. throw SyntaxError on purpose (user's request: not yet). The storage-app branch decided non-'i' units are powers of 1024; that was NOT adopted here, so don't copy it without asking the billing owner.

2026-11-06: billing-svc: when decimal units (kB, MB, GB...) are added, they must be strict SI powers of 1000 ('1 MB' = 1,000,000 bytes), matching what prettyBytes prints. User's rule for this branch (billing quotes in strict SI); contradicts storage-app's 1024 decision, which does not apply here.

2026-11-06: parseBytes units without the 'i' (kB/KB, MB..YB) are now implemented as powers of 1024 per the storage team decision, with tests and readme/index.d.ts docs; the 'not implemented yet' entry is outdated. Matching stays case-sensitive (e.g. 'mb' throws) - my choice, kept from the binary-unit work.
